extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and practitioners before the Korean Intellectual Property Office and Intellectual Property Trial & Appeal Board
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on eligibility, calculation, excluded periods, and application procedures for extending a patent term in Korea due to delay in registration under the Patent Act and its Enforcement Decree/Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for patent term extension (reference date condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for extension due to delay in registration, the date of registration of a patent right must be later than a reference date for extension (the date four years after the filing date of a patent application or the date three years from the date of requesting examination, whichever is later). The system applies only to patent applications filed after March 15, 2012 (post-KORUS FTA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only when the length of a period (after subtracting applicant-attributable delay) exceeds zero will the patent be eligible for term extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of extension period
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual extension equals '(the length of the period between the reference date for extension and the date of registration of a patent right) – (the length of the period delayed due to reasons attributable to an applicant)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the resulting length is not greater than zero, no extension is granted. Precise calculation of applicant-attributable delay is therefore crucial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: periods of delay attributable to an applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Delays attributable to an applicant mean that procedural delays are caused by an applicant; it does not necessarily refer to cases where the applicant is responsible for all delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 7-2 of the Enforcement Decree specifies types of procedural delays attributable to an applicant across 41 subparagraphs; the Enforcement Rules add further specific periods. Even if a period falls under those lists, it may be exempted if, considering specific circumstances, the delay is objectively not attributable to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant extension of filing/designated periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant extends the period for filing a petition for trial or the designated period for a patent-related proceeding, the length of the extended period shall be deemed the period of delay attributable to an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant extends a period and then shortens it, the shortened period shall not be deemed a period of delay attributable to an applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interruption/suspension of proceedings due to applicant circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent-related proceeding (examination, trial, etc.) is interrupted or suspended due to circumstances of an applicant (e.g., applicant dies and successor delay), the period from interruption to resumption shall be deemed the period of delay attributable to an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This treats interruptions caused by applicant-side events as deductible from extension calculation unless facts show otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated consultation-reporting period (Article 36(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where consultation results are required to be reported (e.g., when two or more applications for the same invention are filed the same day), the designated period to report the result of consultation shall constitute a period of delay attributable to an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the designated period is shortened at the applicant's request, the shortened length is not deemed applicant delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment orders on formalities or documents (Article 46 / Article 203(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Commissioner or a presiding administrative patent judge orders amendment on irregularities in formalities or on documents, the period designated while ordering amendments shall be deemed the period attributable to an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: if amendment proceedings are completed prior to a request for examination so registration is not delayed, then the designated period is not deemed applicant-attributable; if an amendment order was mistakenly made (no irregularities), the period may not be deemed applicant delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal/ deemed withdrawal of domestic priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Where examination is withheld because of a domestic priority claim and the priority claim is withdrawn or deemed withdrawn, the period during which examination was withheld shall be deemed a period of delay attributable to an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance clarifies that the applicant's choice regarding timing between parent and divisional/related filings can constitute applicant delay and will reduce the extension calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay in determination of expedited examination due to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Where determination on whether an application is to be subject to expedited examination is delayed due to circumstances of an applicant (e.g., amendment ordered on a request for expedited examination or attached documents), the designated period shall be deemed the period of delay attributable to an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it is later found there were no deficiencies in the expedited-exam request, the designated period shall not be deemed applicant-attributable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period allowed for submission of written argument after notice of rejection (Article 63)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner notifies a ground of rejection and gives an applicant an opportunity to submit arguments, the period allowed for the submission of a written argument shall be deemed the period of delay attributable to an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if the examiner recognizes that the ground for rejection was traversed by the applicant's written argument alone (without amendments, withdrawal/abandonment, transfer, etc.) and grants the patent, the designated period shall not constitute applicant-attributable delay. The same applies mutatis mutandis to administrative patent judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of patent fee after service of decision to grant
rubrics_metrics.description: The period between the date of service of a certified copy of a decision to grant a patent and the date when the patent right is registered after the payment of a patent fee shall constitute the period of delay attributable to an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes late payment, payment of remaining fees after the period has elapsed, or payment under Article 81(3). If an applicant is exempted from payment under Article 83, the period between service and exemption (after submitting required documents) shall be deemed applicant delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reexamination after decision to reject
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant amends specification/drawings and then requests reexamination, the period between the date of service of a certified copy of a decision to reject and the date when a request for reexamination is made shall be deemed the period of delay attributable to an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: if the applicant could have addressed the rejection by amendment initially but instead requested reexamination, that intervening period counts as applicant delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay in service of documents due to unclear applicant/agent address
rubrics_metrics.description: Where service of documents is delayed because the address or business address of an applicant or representative is unclear, the length of the delay for service of documents shall be the period of delay attributable to an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: failure to report address change that causes return and re-service — the delay between when the applicant would have received the copy had they reported the change and the date they actually received it is applicant-attributable delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of decision to grant at applicant's request (Enforcement Rules / Article 40-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner defers the decision to grant a patent at the request of an applicant, the period between the date when the applicant submitted a request for deferral and the date when twelve months have elapsed from the date of filing a patent application shall be deemed applicant delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as part of Enforcement Rules item; relates to deferral choices made by applicants that extend time to registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of examination at applicant's request (Article 40-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner defers examination at the request of an applicant, the period between the date when the applicant made the request and the desired expiration date of deferral (or changed date) shall be deemed the period of delay attributable to an applicant. If the applicant withdraws the request for deferral, only the period up to withdrawal is deemed applicant delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If desired expiration date is changed, the changed date becomes the new date for calculation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 54(5) Enforcement Rules: specified applicant-caused periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Period prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Knowledge Economy' under Article 7-2(1)(iv) includes: (1) designated periods to submit electronic documents when ordered; (2) designated periods to explain when ordered to submit evidential documents; (3) periods for explanation when returning application documents deemed illegitimate; (4) deferral of decision to grant at applicant's request; (5) deferral of examination at applicant's request; (6) periods to amend litigation documents or submit answer briefs to meet formality requirements; (7) other periods delayed due to any request, amendment or submission made by the applicant in patent-related proceedings or related litigation/administrative proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some of these items overlap with other listed types; they are recognized explicitly in the Enforcement Rules as periods attributable to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-caused delays in litigation and administrative appeal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In litigation proceedings appealing trial decisions or administrative appeals, applicant-attributable delays include: periods where a disqualification/recusal request is not accepted and proceedings are suspended; designated periods for amendment to litigation capabilities or right of representation or complaint deficiencies; periods between an initial hearing date and a newly designated hearing date when applicant failed to appear or argue; and periods between request for evidential documents and a date when such evidence is decided unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays caused by requests, amendments, or submissions by applicants in administrative appeal or litigation proceedings are treated analogously and can reduce extension entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions: circumstances exempting listed delays from being applicant-attributable
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a period falls under listed applicant-attributable items, it shall not be deemed applicant-attributable where, considering specific circumstances, such delay is objectively not attributable to the applicant. Examples: (i) delay occurred before a request for examination and did not affect registration delay; (ii) amendment order/notification was mistakenly made by the Office; (iii) delay caused by natural disasters or other non-applicant reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative examples: amendment order and subsequent proceedings completed before request for examination (case i); amendment order mistakenly made but later found no irregularities (case ii); interruption due to natural disasters (case iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date rules for divisional/converted/international applications in extension calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the 'date four years after filing' reference date: the actual filing date of a divisional application, a converted application, or an application by a legitimate right holder (or international filing date for international applications) shall be deemed the filing date. Periods between parent filing date and actual filing of divisional/ national phase entry are considered applicant choice and thus reduce extension calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because applicant choices about divisionaling or national phase entry can consume time, those periods will be treated as applicant-attributable unless facts show otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirements and timing for registration of patent term extension (Article 92-3 / Enforcement Rules 54-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for registration of patent term extension must state: applicant name and domicile (or corporate name and office), agent name/location (if any), patent number, period of application for extension, and grounds for extension with evidential materials attached. The application must be filed within three months from the date of registration of the patent right. Joint owners must file together. Power of attorney required if a representative conducts the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may amend items 4 (period of application) and 5 (grounds/evidence) before an examiner decides; after receipt of notice of grounds for rejection, amendments are allowed only during the period for submission of arguments (mutatis mutandis Article 93). Annexed Form 30-2 and specified attachments required under Enforcement Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for extension per Enforcement Rules (Article 54-3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds designated under Ordinance (Ministry of Knowledge Economy) include: (1) registration occurred after four years from filing or three years from request for examination (whichever later); (2) the period requested for extension and explanation showing applicant-attributable delays have been reduced from that period plus evidential documents; (3) other necessary items to prove the ground for extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must attach a copy of evidential documents proving the extension ground and any explanation showing how applicant-attributable delays were accounted for.
